name: High-Press 4-4-2

slots.why: Distributes to the forwards or wide midfielders after winning the ball.
Support full-back gives width and pushes up to join the press on the flank.
Central defender. Cover is the alternate.
Central defender on the right. Cover is the alternate, but only one Cover can be used.
Support full-back on the right, doing the same job as on the left.
Wide midfielder (Support) works hard to close the full-back and gives the team width when the ball is won.
Ball-winning midfielder harries the opposition midfield and wins the ball for the forwards.
Box-to-box midfielder supports the press and runs beyond the forwards.
Wide midfielder (Support) on the right, doing the same job as on the left.
Pressing forward (Defend) starts the press and drops back to help the midfield, so he is the workhorse of the pair.
Pressing forward (Attack) presses too, but stays higher and looks to run in behind when the ball is won.

description: A 4-4-2 that presses from the front with two pressing forwards, a ball-winning midfielder and a box-to-box runner, and hard-working wide midfielders.
whyGood: Two forwards pressing the centre-backs, backed by a midfield that presses together, wins the ball high with a simple, easy-to-understand shape.
whyThisShape: Two pressing forwards start the press by closing the centre-backs and goalkeeper, and the ball-winner and box-to-box midfielder support them, so the whole team compresses the opponent's build-up. The 4-4-2 is compact, so the distances between players are short and the press is easy to keep together.
whenToUse: When you have fit, energetic forwards and midfielders and want to press the opponent's build-up, especially against a side that plays short from the back.
whenNotToUse: Against sides that play long over the press, or when your players are tired: a two-man press leaves gaps behind it if it is beaten.

instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Starts the press in the opponent's half so the ball is won high.
instructionRationale.Much More Urgent Pressing: Presses with more intensity, which wins the ball more often but tires the team.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Presses at once after losing the ball, so possession is regained before the opponent settles.
instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Gets the ball forward quickly to the forwards when it is won.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Moves the ball quickly while the opponent is out of shape.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: A balanced line rather than a high one, so the two-man press does not leave the defence exposed.

keyRequirements: Two forwards with high stamina and work rate to initiate the press
Central midfielders with the engine and aggression to support the first line
Wide midfielders who can repeatedly recover and press the flanks
Full-backs fit enough to step forward behind the wide midfielders
Enough squad depth and fitness to sustain the intensity across a season
